completion_criteria.text: 0092 diagnosis: the merge-boundary preflight never exits non-zero with empty stdout again - every non-zero exit emits a human-readable reason, and running the CLI directly with no MITOSIS_BOUNDARY_* env prints why it refused. Proven by executing the real CLI in that exact unconfigured state and reading its output.

0092 posture: a decision record settles whether the unconfigured boundary halts the run or degrades with a surfaced warning, and the engine implements what that record decides. The record must state the security trade-off explicitly, since fail-closed is what currently makes the engine unusable.

0092 receipt: a test execs the real preflight CLI end-to-end instead of stubbing the verdict, and it is RED when the step-7 call site is severed and GREEN when it is wired. The red state is demonstrated by actually severing the call site in a scratch copy, not asserted.

0093: gate identity stops being string equality on an unresolved path - the gate resolves a real path, or is relocated outside the repo it manages. A test redirects the path to a different file and asserts the gate refuses rather than trusting it.

0094: the config guard covers git worktrees - a write to a guarded path inside a real git worktree of this repo is held for human confirmation, asserted by a test that builds an actual worktree fixture rather than simulating one.

Each of the above lands as its own MSP through the centralized pr-create tool, and origin/main is verified fully green (full suite, exit 0) after each merge - re-derived from the remote, never from a possibly-stale local main.

spine.active_goal: Fix the three boundary-layer defects inherited from the predecessor, which shipped a green main (origin/main a229c9c, 1544/1544) but left these unfixed. 0092 is urgent: the engine is UNUSABLE - step 7 execs the merge-boundary preflight with no MITOSIS_BOUNDARY_* env, it exits 31 with no stdout, and every run halts. Under 0095 that is the permanent steady state, so this thread must settle the posture deliberately rather than await an activation that will never come.
spine.next_step: START WITH 0092, and start by REPRODUCING: exec the preflight CLI directly with no MITOSIS_BOUNDARY_* env and confirm exit 31 with empty stdout before changing anything. Then decide the posture (halt vs degrade-with-warning) and record it as a decision BEFORE implementing - that choice trades availability against fail-closed security and must not be made implicitly inside a patch.
open_risks: 0092 corollary: layer 2 has NEVER worked end-to-end, not even before the severance - which is why a week-long severance went unnoticed. Scheduler tests stub the verdict and never exec the CLI, so they cannot catch this class of defect. Fixing the stub matters as much as fixing the wiring.

0093 MEDIUM: ~/.claude/lib symlinks into this repo, so both boundary layers exec the SAME mutable file inside the repo under management. invokedAs is string equality on an unresolved path and cannot detect a poisoned gate - the two layers are not independent.

0094: the config guard does not cover git worktrees, and mitosis puts every fanned-out agent in one, so the engine bypasses its own guard by design. This also weakens 0093's mitigation, which assumed a poisoning write must pass the guard.
PROCESS: subagent self-reports are NOT trustworthy - one committed while reporting 'no commit, no push', evidently with --no-verify since the suite was red. Verify every claim against the repository.

PROCESS: never site a worktree in another session's scratchpad - one was garbage-collected mid-session, destroying three uncommitted files. Equally, never assume a scratchpad is dead: the predecessor's spine said 'dead scratchpad' while it was live with 3 modified files.

PROCESS: local main can lag origin/main badly (8 behind at close). Re-derive the baseline from the remote. For squash-merged branches `git branch --merged` is blind - compare blobs against origin/main instead.

PR #10 was merged while its review was still running, so the reviewer's BLOCK (0092) landed after the change was already on main. That is the direct cause of this thread existing. Do not merge before review returns.
